about.heroTitle: From a living-room meeting to a governed institution.
about.heroSubline: How a handful of Ikeduru's sons and daughters turned conviction into a working forum for economic development.
about.visionText: An economically and socially vibrant, prosperous, and self-sustaining Ikeduru, where the collective expertise, resources, and commitment of its people drive transformative and inclusive development.
about.missionText: To mobilize the collective expertise, resources, and partnerships of Ikeduru people and stakeholders to advance sustainable economic growth, attract investment, strengthen communities, and improve the quality of life through innovative, inclusive, and collaborative development initiatives.
about.missionImageAlt: IEDF Mission infographic illustrating five pillars: Mobilize, Advance, Attract Investment, Strengthen Communities, and Improve Quality of Life, under the theme Collaborate, Innovate, Invest, Prosper
about.lLeadTitle: Meet the people driving the mission
about.lLeadText: The executive committee — professionals from medicine, law, accountancy, technology and industry, spanning three continents.
about.apoliticalText: IEDF is a non-governmental, non-profit, and apolitical organization. Our work is guided solely by the economic development interests of Ikeduru — independent of any political party or affiliation.
about.storyP1: Despite its proximity to Owerri, the Imo State capital, Ikeduru Local Government Area (LGA) has remained sleepy economically with no meaningful development in the last thirty years. The economic neglect of Ikeduru and lack of local opportunities despite its potential has led to mass urban migration of young people in search of greener pasture. The rising poverty, poor educational amenities, lack of health and security infrastructure among other challenges have remained evident across Ikeduru for decades.
about.storyP2: IEDF is a non-governmental, non-profit, apolitical community development organisation made up of select Ikeduru sons and daughters who are genuinely committed to the development of the locality through incubation of ideas, collaboration, promotion of innovation and building investment capacity.
about.storyP3: Realising the dwindling fortunes of Ikeduru LGA, lack of government presence and poor government and private sector infrastructure investment in the locality, men and women of Ikeduru LGA came together to chart a new developmental course for the LGA with emphasis on private sector led investment and advocacy for government attention in areas of need. This led to the formation of IEDF on 4th January 2025. The inaugural meeting was held at Umuoziri Inyishi at the country home of Mr. Decency Nwokedi, and in attendance were the following Ikeduru indigenes: Rt. Hon. Justice Nze (Ikeduru LGA Chairman), Mr. Decency Nwokedi (USA), Mr. Evan Agunanne (USA), Dr. Goddy Ike (USA), Mr. Bede Anunne (USA), and Dr. Pedus Eweama (Australia). It has since then attracted major Ikeduru stakeholders at home and in the diaspora.
about.storyP4: Ikeduru Economic Development Forum since inception has acted as a think tank and resource entity for investors interested in Ikeduru. It has continued to engage people from Ikeduru resident across the world who are genuinely and apolitically committed to the advancement of important developmental priorities across Ikeduru. It seeks to continue to engage well-meaning Ikeduru sons and daughters to think of and invest in Ikeduru, with the conviction that only Ikeduru people can champion its development. Ultimately, IEDF will continue to collaborate with government and private sector investors in seeking opportunities for investment in various areas of economic endeavour, including agro-allied industries, small scale food processing centres, and investment in health, security, and education.
about.storyP5: With the support of the current leadership of Ikeduru LGA under the chairmanship of Rt. Hon. Justice Nze, parts of the Atta-Inyishi-Amaimo axis have been designated an industrial cluster for Ikeduru, which will amplify economic activities within this corridor. Courtesy of IEDF, a startup electricity generating company is exploring ways of using gas to generate electricity to feed the emerging businesses within the newly approved industrial cluster and beyond. IEDF aims to collaborate with Imo State government through the Office of the Chief Economic Advisor to advance One Kindred, One Business Initiative (OKOBI), a home grown, Imo State government backed economic model that can drive economic growth through support for small and medium scale group and community owned enterprises.

aboutIkeduru.heroSubline: The heartland — distinct from IEDF, the organization. History, people, and economic life across Ikeduru LGA, Imo State.
aboutIkeduru.historyP1: The land the world now calls Ikeduru has been home to Igbo-speaking communities for centuries. As across most of Igboland, its earliest layers of history rest on oral tradition — ancestral founder lineages, kindred groups, age grades and market cycles — rather than on dated written records. What the record does show clearly is a people organised around self-governing village-groups, clan institutions, title societies and shared market days, long before colonial administrators arrived.
aboutIkeduru.historyP2: Ikeduru sits in the western part of Imo State, in Nigeria's South East. It is bounded on the north by Isiala Mbano, on the south by Owerri North, and on the west by Aboh Mbaise and Ahiazu Mbaise — with its former twin, Mbaitoli, alongside it to the east. Its administrative headquarters is the town of Iho (Iho-Dimeze), on the Owerri–Okigwe road.
aboutIkeduru.historyP3: For most of the twentieth century, the communities of Ikeduru fell within Owerri Province under colonial administration. After Nigeria's independence in 1960, and the creation of Imo State in 1976, the area passed through successive local-government reorganisations. In 1989, the then Mbaitoli/Ikeduru Local Government Area was divided in two, making Ikeduru a local government area in its own right, with headquarters at Iho.
aboutIkeduru.historyP4: The Ikeduru people are Igbo. Farming remains an anchor of local life — cassava, yam, cocoyam and maize — but the area is best known for its palm produce: Ikeduru has long been a regional centre for palm-oil processing and trade, a tradition studies trace back generations in communities such as Owalla-Avuvu. Community records also note mineral deposits — limestone, kaolin, silica sand among them — and a history of local industry, from garri and palm-kernel mills to small manufacturing outfits.
aboutIkeduru.historyP5: Ikeduru is home to a dense web of schools — mission-founded and community-built — including Archbishop Pepple Seminary at Inyishi and Umuoziri Technical Secondary School in Umuoziri. Its health infrastructure has grown alongside: the Ikeduru Hospital Complex at Iho, on KM 13 of the Owerri–Okigwe road, anchors specialist facilities, among them the American Cancer Hospital, a subsidiary of Imo International Health Systems.
aboutIkeduru.historyP6: The landscape itself carries the culture: the Eke Omumiri hills along the Amakohia–Owubinubi axis, the Uzoagba–Eziama hills, Onu-Oha and Onu-Ngara at Okwu and Avuvu, the Ugirike–Obohia hills — and the confluence of the Mba and Oramiri-Ukwu at Avuvu. The festival calendar keeps towns bound together: the new-yam feast (Iriji), Mmanwu masquerades, Igba Nta, Okposhi, Isuachara, Egwuonwa, Omugwo and others.
aboutIkeduru.historyP7: Ikeduru has also sent its sons and daughters far beyond its hills — among them the late Sir Emmanuel Iwuanyanwu, the Atta-born businessman, engineer and statesman, and scholars and public servants such as Professor Placid Njoku. Their journeys recall the conviction on which this forum was founded: that Ikeduru's greatest asset is Ikeduru people.
aboutIkeduru.historyP8: This history is distilled from public and community sources (listed below). In keeping with IEDF's apolitical charter, political events and office-holders are deliberately excluded. IEDF invites corrections from official LGA records and community historians — such corrections will be dated and incorporated.

aboutIkeduru.hqP1: The administrative headquarters of Ikeduru Local Government Area is the town of Iho (also written Ihuo or Iho-Dimeze), on the Owerri–Okigwe road in western Imo State.
aboutIkeduru.hqP2: Ikeduru became a local government area in its own right in 1989, when the former Mbaitoli/Ikeduru LGA was divided. It is organised into twelve wards and twenty-nine autonomous communities, each with its traditional stool.
aboutIkeduru.hqP3: This section describes civic geography only. Sitting elected officials are omitted on purpose — IEDF's charter is apolitical. For traditional leadership, see the communities list below.
aboutIkeduru.econP1: Farming anchors everyday life across Ikeduru — cassava, yam, cocoyam and maize — while palm produce remains the area's best-known commercial tradition, with processing and trade rooted in communities such as Owalla-Avuvu for generations.
aboutIkeduru.econP2: Community records also note mineral deposits including limestone, kaolin and silica sand, alongside a history of small local industry: garri and palm-kernel mills, and modest manufacturing outfits serving nearby markets.
aboutIkeduru.econP3: Proximity to Owerri gives Ikeduru a corridor advantage. Parts of the Atta–Inyishi–Amaimo axis have been designated an industrial cluster, and IEDF is supporting gas-to-power exploration to serve emerging businesses along that corridor — see Projects.
aboutIkeduru.econP4: IEDF also collaborates toward Imo State's One Kindred, One Business Initiative (OKOBI), a group- and community-enterprise model. Figures for output volumes, employment shares, or investment totals are not published here until named official datasets are available.

leadership.heroSubline: The executive committee — seasoned professionals across medicine, law, accountancy, technology and industry, united by a single purpose.
leadership.bio1a: Dr. Pedus Eweama serves as President of IEDF, having been the vision bearer for its formation. A medical practitioner from Umuofor Autonomous Community, Amaimo, he is an award-winning leader in the Nigerian diaspora community, having led various diaspora organisations in Australia.
leadership.bio1b: He is Founder and CEO of G-Prest Imperial Limited, makers of Ginika Feed products in Inyishi, Ikeduru — Imo State's only fully automated fish and poultry feed factory. In 2025, NIDCOM honored him with Nigeria's National Diaspora Merit Award.
leadership.bio2a: High Chief Dozie Ononiwu, FICP, serves as Vice President of IEDF. FICP denotes Certified Fellow of the Institute of Cooperative Professionals of Nigeria (ICOPRON). A native of Amatta, he is an entrepreneur with diverse business interests, as well as a community leader and philanthropist.
leadership.bio2b: His commitment to Ikeduru includes a public-private partnership investment in the Brookside Transportation Hub (Ama Nwaozuzu Park) in Iho, and the development of Food Grotto, an oil palm processing facility in his community of Amatta. He is married with children.
leadership.bio3a: Okeys Ononiwu serves as Secretary of IEDF. An accomplished technology executive and business transformation leader with extensive international experience, he hails from Amatta, Ikeduru.
leadership.bio3b: He is Founder and Chairman of the Okeys Ononiwu Youth Empowerment Foundation (OOYEF), supporting young people through education, scholarships, and mentorship.
leadership.bio4a: Evans Agunanne serves as Treasurer of IEDF. A native of Inyishi, Ikeduru, he is a practicing Medical Laboratory Scientist and Director of Evans Biomedics Laboratory Nigeria.
leadership.bio4b: He runs Evans Biomedics Learning, an online tutoring platform helping lab scientists prepare for internationally recognized certifications, and uses Ikemba Farms to introduce bioagriculture to youths across Imo State.
leadership.bio5a: Tonie Eweama serves as Chief Whip of IEDF. He hails from Umuofor Autonomous Community in the Amaimo ancient kingdom, and currently lives and works in Australia, where he manages an export business focused on the automotive industry and accessories.
leadership.bio5b: He is also involved in various community development initiatives at home, with special interest in upskilling indigent young people to become self-reliant.
leadership.bio6a: Mr. Bede Anunne serves as Financial Secretary of IEDF. A native of Inyishi, he is a highly accomplished professional accountant with extensive local and international affiliations.
leadership.bio6b: He is a member of both the Institute of Chartered Accountants of Nigeria and the Nigerian Institute of Taxation.
leadership.bio7a: Joe Erekaha serves as Assistant Secretary of IEDF. A native of Amaku Akabo, Ikeduru LGA, he is a Health Practitioner resident in Australia.
leadership.bio7b: He is active in community leadership, including the Nigerian Association of WA Inc. and the Council of Nigeria Association Presidents in Australia Inc., with key interests in health enlightenment and leadership awareness.
leadership.bio8a: Hon. Dr. Lady Clara Nwakaego Njoku, JP, serves as Public Relations Officer of IEDF and is the Honorable Commissioner, Imo State House of Assembly Service Commission. A native of Ikeduru LGA, she holds a PhD in Conflict Resolution and an MSc in International Relations from Imo State University.
leadership.bio8b: She is Founder of Rejoice International Foundation, an NGO supporting women, widows, and persons with disabilities across all 27 LGAs of Imo State, and has served in several public and community leadership roles, including Transition Chairman of Ikeduru LGA and President of Women, Anglican Communion Ikeduru. She holds the chieftaincy titles Igolo of Ogbor and Nwanyi Puruichie of Umunkwo.
leadership.bio9a: Chigozie George Iwuoha, Esq., serves as Legal Adviser to IEDF. A Legal Practitioner from Amaimo, Ikeduru, he currently serves as Head of Legal Services at the National Salaries, Incomes and Wages Commission.
leadership.bio9b: He is a community leader actively involved in grassroots development initiatives in Ikeduru.

news.postFoundedTitle: IEDF is founded in Umuoziri Inyishi
news.postFoundedSummary: On 4 January 2025, Ikeduru sons and daughters at home and in the diaspora formed the Ikeduru Economic Development Forum.
news.postFoundedP1: IEDF was formed on 4 January 2025 at the country home of Mr. Decency Nwokedi in Umuoziri Inyishi. The inaugural circle brought together Ikeduru indigenes connecting Nigeria, the United States, and Australia around one conviction: Ikeduru's development must be championed by Ikeduru people.
news.postFoundedP2: From the first meeting, the forum set itself apart as a non-governmental, non-profit, and apolitical body — focused on private-sector-led investment, community advocacy, and the incubation of ideas that turn latent potential into opportunity.
news.postFoundedP3: The founding opened a channel for diaspora-home collaboration that has since drawn stakeholders across three continents into the work of building a self-sustaining Ikeduru.
news.postClusterTitle: Industrial cluster designated on the Atta–Inyishi–Amaimo axis
news.postClusterSummary: Parts of the Atta–Inyishi–Amaimo corridor are designated an industrial cluster for agro-allied growth in Ikeduru.
news.postClusterP1: With support from Ikeduru LGA leadership, parts of the Atta–Inyishi–Amaimo axis have been designated an industrial cluster — a catalytic corridor for agro-allied industry and related enterprise.
news.postClusterP2: IEDF has acted as a think tank and resource entity around the designation, connecting investor interest to the opportunity and advocating for the infrastructure the corridor needs to thrive.
news.postClusterP3: In parallel, a startup electricity generating company is exploring gas-to-power options to serve emerging businesses within the cluster and beyond. Details live on the Projects page.
news.postInaugurationSummary: In April 2026, IEDF inaugurated its executive committee — professionals spanning medicine, law, accountancy, technology, and industry.
news.postInaugurationP1: In April 2026, the Ikeduru Economic Development Forum inaugurated its executive committee, moving from founding circle to a governed institution with clear roles and accountability.
news.postInaugurationP2: The nine-member committee brings together professionals across medicine, law, accountancy, technology, and industry — spanning Nigeria, the United States, and Australia — united by a single developmental purpose.
news.postInaugurationP3: Profiles of the committee are published on the Leadership & Governance page. The inauguration marks the forum's readiness to steward active initiatives and the 2026–2029 strategic roadmap.

privacy.heroSubline: How we collect, store, and use information you share with IEDF through this website.
privacy.introText:
The Ikeduru Economic Development Forum (IEDF) is a non-governmental, non-profit, apolitical organisation working toward a self-sustaining Ikeduru, Imo State, Nigeria. This website is operated for IEDF by Okeys Ononiwu Consulting.

This policy explains what personal information we collect through the site, why we collect it, how we store it, and the choices you have. It applies to www.iedf.org.ng and related staging hosts used to operate the site.
privacy.collectText:
We collect information you voluntarily submit through our forms:

• Contact form — name, email, optional organisation, inquiry type, and message.
• Member / volunteer / giving-interest form — name (optional on giving interest), email, and area of interest.
• Newsletter form — email address.

We also receive standard technical data that web servers and hosting providers typically log (for example IP address, browser type, and request timestamps) when you visit the site. We do not sell personal data.
privacy.useText:
We use submitted information to:

• Respond to inquiries and route them to the appropriate IEDF contact.
• Follow up on membership, volunteering, and giving interest.
• Send occasional newsletter updates about IEDF's work (if you subscribed).
• Maintain the security and reliability of the website.

We do not use your information for unrelated marketing by third parties.
privacy.storeText:
Form submissions are stored in a managed Postgres database hosted by Neon. Internal notification emails about new submissions are sent through Resend to an IEDF administrative address.

Hosting for the website may be provided by platforms such as Vercel. Those providers process data under their own security and privacy commitments as our processors.
privacy.shareText:
We share personal information only with service providers who help us operate the site (database hosting, email delivery, and website hosting), and only as needed for those services.

We may also disclose information if required by applicable law or to protect the rights, safety, and integrity of IEDF and its members.
privacy.retainText:
We keep form submissions for as long as needed to respond to you and to maintain a responsible record of organisational correspondence. Newsletter addresses are kept until you ask to be removed.

You may request deletion of your submission or newsletter subscription by contacting us using the details below.
privacy.rightsText:
Depending on where you live, you may have rights to access, correct, or delete personal information we hold about you, or to object to certain processing. To exercise these rights, email the address in the Contact section below.

You can unsubscribe from the newsletter by emailing us with the subject line “Unsubscribe”.
privacy.childrenText: This website and its forms are intended for adults engaging with IEDF's development work. We do not knowingly collect personal information from children under 16. If you believe a child has submitted information, contact us and we will delete it.
privacy.changesText: We may update this policy as our practices or legal requirements evolve. The “Last updated” date at the top of this page will change when we do. Material changes will be reflected on this page.
privacy.contactUsText:
For privacy questions or requests, use the Contact page on this website or email the administrative address published for IEDF correspondence.

If a formal legal review later requires amendments, those amendments will replace the relevant sections here and the update date will be revised.
